name: Sealos DevBox

modes.label: Monthly resource package (flat, shared by all DevBoxes/apps in the plan)
modes.commit_note: Flat monthly price for a fixed resource package; the same price whether DevBoxes run 1 h or 730 h. No overage: allocating more than the package requires a manual upgrade. Disk and traffic caps per tier are in the tier names.
modes.note: Plan capacity is what you can allocate at once (sum of DevBox/app CPU and memory), shared with managed DBs and object storage. Whether a sleeping (normal shutdown) DevBox still holds its CPU/RAM against the package is undocumented; it does keep its NodePort. [basis verified 2026-09-28] Confirmed flat allocation package (pool mode, basis fields ignored): "Your plan price covers the resources listed on the plan card ... allocating more resources requires a manual plan upgrade" (sealos.io/pricing). No usage metering.

modes.label: New-user price on first paid plan (Starter $7, Hobby $25)
modes.commit_note: 'First paid plan purchase · Eligibility confirmed in Cost Center'. Whether it recurs after the first month is not stated.
modes.note: Promotional; flag 'promo' (non-standard) so the engine only prices it on opt-in.

plans.name: Monthly resource package
plans.note: The package price is carried by the pool modes (fee 0 here to avoid double counting). AI credits bundled: 100 / 300 / 800 on Starter / Hobby / Standard.

plans.name: Custom
plans.note: 'A resource package and support plan built around your needs' — contact sales.

caveats: Not a metered sandbox: flat monthly resource packages with no overage. Traffic (10GB-10TB) and disk (10-1024Gi) caps are per tier; exceeding needs an upgrade. Engine egress/disk fields left null because allowances are tier-bound.
Starter/Hobby give only 1 GiB RAM per vCPU; a 4 vCPU / 8 GiB DevBox needs Standard ($128) or larger.
Whether an account can stack several packages (e.g. 4 x Team instead of Enterprise) is not documented.

No pay-as-you-go option is published any more. The 'CPU $40 / RAM $20 / Volume $3 / Egress $2.50' figures that search engines attribute to Sealos are Railway's rates from Sealos's comparison calculator ($20/avg vCPU, $10/avg GB, $0.15/GB volume, $0.05/GB egress, verified 2026-08-21) and must not be used for Sealos.
New-user price ($7 Starter, $25 Hobby) applies to the 'first paid plan purchase'; recurrence unclear. Modeled as a separate 'promo'-flagged pool mode.
7-day no-card free trial (4 vCPU, 4GB, 5GB storage, 500MB bandwidth, 100 AI credits); not represented as credit.
Sleeping DevBoxes keep their NodePort against the quota; whether CPU/RAM stay reserved is undocumented.
Isolation is Kubernetes containers. Regions not published on sealos.io; separate China cloud (sealos.run, CNY) not researched.
Self-hosted Sealos is source-available (Sealos Sustainable Use License), not OSI open source.

Plans are aggregate resource pools, not one sandbox of the displayed size: 50 concurrent 4 vCPU / 8 GiB workers need 200 vCPU / 400 GiB allocated at once, so the smallest fitting published pool is Enterprise ($12,451/mo); low CPU utilisation does not shrink the allocation. Taxes/optional services billed separately in Cost Center. (patch v10-regional, 2026-09-28)

Some Sealos docs (llms.txt 'How Much Does It Cost?' section) still list Starter $7 / Hobby $25 as the plain monthly prices; the live pricing page shows these only as first-purchase new-user prices (regular $34 / $70). Use the pricing page.

fleet.verification: Seven-day trial no card required; new-user paid promotional eligibility confirmed in Cost Center.
fleet.tiers: Trial 4 vCPU/4 GB/5 GB storage; paid fixed resource packages with higher aggregate pools; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: No published instance count. Trial at 4 vCPU/8 GiB workload is insufficient memory. Paid package pool limits must be checked for each fleet; multiple concurrent package stacking not documented. 10/50/300/1,000 machines not derivable without shape and pool choice.
